2026-11-20 Milestone Progression

Lower-Body Hypertrophy & Back Squat Milestone Consolidation

✓ IMPROVED
Trigger: ATHX 2027 Back Squat Benchmark Progression (+0.47 kg/wk required velocity)
Physiological 'Why' Rationale: With Quads entering the optimal MAV band (16.1 sets/wk trailing 4-week mesocycle) and systemic ACWR holding in the Sweet Spot (1.20), heavy mechanical tension exposure was scheduled. Executing 3 working reps @ 102.1 kg locked in an estimated 1RM of 112.3 kg, compressing the qualification deficit to -12.7 kg while verifying zero patellar or articular strain.
Pre-Intervention Baseline Historical Squat e1RM: 101.3 kg · Large Benchmark Deficit (-23.7 kg) · 30-week Diluted Volume (9.2 sets/wk)
Post-Intervention Result Nov 20 Back Squat: 112.3 kg e1RM (+11.0 kg gain) · Quads 16.1 sets/wk (MAV zone) · ACWR 1.20 Sweet Spot · Gap -12.7 kg
● Back Squat velocity (+0.47 kg/wk) tracking ahead of qualification timeline with balanced neuromuscular fatigue.
2026-11-19 Volume Infusion

Upper Push & Pull MEV Deficit Remediation Infusion

✓ OPTIMIZED
Trigger: AI Coach Volume Deficit Alert (Chest volume 8.1 sets/wk, 19% below 10.0 MEV floor; Triceps below MAV)
Physiological 'Why' Rationale: Telemetry triage revealed persistent upper push volume starvation (-19% below MEV in chest volume) directly limiting Shoulder-to-Overhead (S2O) progression. Capitalizing on a peak parasympathetic supercompensation window (Garmin HRV 70 ms, BALANCED), a high-density 31-set upper hypertrophy session was injected targeting chest, triceps, and horizontal pulling.
Pre-Intervention Baseline Chest Volume: 8.1 sets/wk (Sub-MEV Deficit) · Triceps 9.1 sets/wk (Sub-MAV) · S2O Deficit -6.7 kg
Post-Intervention Result Nov 19 Session: 31 working sets (9.05 tons) · Bench Press (90 kg e1RM) + Shoulder Press loaded · Triceps 106.7 kg e1RM · Pre-HRV 70 ms
● Upper push MEV deficit remediated; pressing mechanical tension restored without autonomic depression.
2026-11-12 Peak Capacity

Posterior Chain Load Progression & Deadlift All-Time Peak

✓ IMPROVED

This opened a low-fatigue window for neural drive and heavy floor pulling. Heavy deadlift triples drove central motor drive efficiency, achieving an all-time personal best 151.7 kg e1RM.

2026-11-11 Durability Strain

Hero WOD 'Chad' Eccentric Durability Load Management

✓ OPTIMIZED
Trigger: High-Volume Eccentric Muscular Endurance Stimulus (1,000 Weighted Box Step-Ups)
Physiological 'Why' Rationale: Hero WOD 'Chad' introduces 1,000 unilateral eccentric knee extension cycles, posing acute delayed-onset muscular damage (DOMS) and patellar tendon fatigue risks. Pacing was managed to prevent premature peripheral muscle failure, followed by aggressive recovery protocols (hydration, restorative sleep) to monitor systemic autonomic tolerance.
Pre-Intervention Baseline High-Risk Unilateral Muscular Endurance Challenge · Potential Sympathetic Fatigue Crash & ACWR Spike
Post-Intervention Result 1,000 Step-Ups completed · Zero tendon degradation · Overnight HRV climbed from 59 ms to 70 ms (Nov 11) & 79 ms (Nov 12)
● Massive work-rate durability validated; autonomic nervous system fully absorbed eccentric strain.
2026-11-06 Threshold Architecture

Critical Speed (CS) Pacing Threshold Lock

✓ IMPROVED
Trigger: 5km Aerobic Pace Benchmark (+42s/km gap vs 4:30 ATHX qualification)
Physiological 'Why' Rationale: Running above Critical Speed (3.16 m/s / 5:16/km) drains the finite 156.8m D' battery, inducing metabolic acidosis and cellular fatigue that directly blunts subsequent heavy squat hypertrophic adaptation. Capping continuous aerobic running at CS allows mitochondrial biogenesis while isolating high-velocity sprint capacity to controlled 1k repeats.
Pre-Intervention Baseline Historical 5k Pace: 5:41/km · GCT 307.6 ms · Anaerobic fatigue leakage
Post-Intervention Result Nov 6 Paris Run: 4.71 km @ 5:12/km · Fastest 1k split 4:05/km · GCT 257.7 ms · D' battery protected
● +29s/km velocity progression with optimized ground contact (257.7 ms) and zero systemic interference.
2026-11-04 Active Recovery

Autonomic Protection & Active Deload Shift

✓ OPTIMIZED
Trigger: Morning Health Check (Garmin Overnight HRV plunged to 28 ms vs 52 ms baseline)
Physiological 'Why' Rationale: A steep overnight drop in Garmin HRV (28 ms, UNBALANCED) signals acute sympathetic dominance and blunted vagal reactivation. Executing high-glycolytic conditioning in this compromised state blunts muscle protein synthesis (mTOR) and degrades power output. Substituted high-intensity work with tissue recovery and restorative sleep.
